The `source` array downloads the AppImage and LICENSE file from the project's official GitHub repository using HTTPS. The URLs are constructed predictably from `pkgver`, which is hardcoded, so there is no risk of dynamic code execution or unexpected payload fetching during sourcing. The `sha256sums` are provided and match the sources, though even if they were 'SKIP', that would not make this phase unsafe—extraction without execution is expected behavior.

No command substitution, `eval`, or executable logic appears in the global scope. The `prepare()` and `package()` functions contain logic that runs later (after this gate), such as extracting the AppImage and setting permissions, but these are not executed under `--noprepare` and `--nobuild`. Therefore, sourcing the PKGBUILD and fetching sources pose no risk of unintended code execution or data exfiltration.
</details>

<details>
The PKGBUILD defines two sources: an AppImage binary from the project's GitHub release page and the LICENSE file from the upstream repository. Both are fetched over HTTPS from GitHub (github.com/pingdotgg/t3code), which is the expected upstream source. The `sha256sums` array contains valid checksums for both files, so the integrity of the downloaded assets will be verified during extraction — though that verification occurs after download, it does not affect the safety of `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare`.

The only executable code outside of the `prepare()` and `package()` functions is the definition of `_appimage` and string interpolation in `source`, which is static and does not involve command substitution or external execution. The `pkgver` is hardcoded, so no dynamic version fetching occurs. There is no top-level shell code, no use of `eval`, `curl|bash`, `base64` decoding, or network exfiltration attempts during sourcing.

Since `--noprepare` and `--nobuild` prevent execution of `prepare()` and `package()`, the actual extraction and manipulation of the AppImage (which could in theory be risky if untrusted) are not performed at this stage. Simply downloading and verifying the sources (even without checksums, which *are* present here) is safe under these flags.

Thus, running `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` on this PKGBUILD poses no risk of executing malicious code during the sourcing or source-fetching phase.
</details>
